content:
Hi everyone. I am an incoming ug student. I am really interested in learning lean. For this purpose i am thinking of going through How to prove it with Lean by Daniel J Velleman.
Since i am starting ug so i don't know lot of math. But i am currently self studying through Apostol calculus , How to prove it by Velleman and Elementary number theory by Burton. Any advice how should i proceed to learn lean would be helpful.

Find yourself a little project (e.g. "solve this exercise in Apostol"), figure out how to state the exercise in Lean (ask here for help or ask an LLM) and then figure out how to prove it (and don't ask the LLM, if you want to learn how to use Lean). Note that "prove" questions are easier for beginners than "calculate" questions.

Thank you for the advice, it was really helpful.
I have one follow-up question. Do you think it's better for a beginner like me to start with Daniel Velleman's book (which uses his custom package), or should I dive straight into learning "normal" Lean 4 and try to formalize small projects from Apostol or Burton right away?
I would just experiment and find what works for you. I strongly encourage people to work on projects of their own ASAP.
Thanks. I would follow your advice and try to work on my project ASAP.
